entry_conditions: The emptied source is securely grasped and particles are already settled. Preference is strongest when the upright source is near the nominal return region or descending, and two-frame geometry can distinguish elevated, supported, open, and retreat phases.
exit_conditions: The source remains upright and stationary at table height inside the return bounds, fingers are open, and the TCP is clear near the demonstrated terminal height of 0.28 m.
overlap_role: All [1460,1740) actions are supervised despite the setdown emphasis, preserving the same 280-action late-righting/outbound overlap with controlled_pour_and_right. This is not a shortened release-only policy.
successor_readiness: This is terminal. Only physical observations of stable upright placement, opening, and clearance indicate readiness for evaluation; auxiliary logits do not.
failure_signatures: Opening while elevated, outside the return region, tilted, or moving; fingers staying closed after stable setdown; source movement after opening; retreat recontact; or IK non-convergence and limit contacts.
continuation_guidance: Near nominal support, continue with repeated causal replans through settling, opening, and upward retreat. Prefer the destination-frame policy for a displaced target and the fresh-TCP policy for a strongly tilted or off-trajectory handoff. Never treat the auxiliary head as a scripted release gate.
limitations: No force/contact truth or failed recovery is present. The auxiliary target is the future demonstrated gripper sign under the framework mask, not support truth, and world-frame output is not displacement invariant.
